doc.title: Lou Donaldson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The Harlem club circuit and its pay
summary: He worked about ten Harlem clubs through a woman named Hilda, earning around 125 dollars a week.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: During the first part of the ‘50s, when you played New York, were you mostly playing in Harlem, or were you playing downtown?
Was there a circuit in Harlem? Describe it a bit.

Well, Harlem was a place where you had to play for the people 100% if you wanted a return engagement. You had to kind of do a little swing. So I got a chance to play at all these clubs. There was a woman around there named Hilda, and she worked... I guess she worked for the Mob—I guess. But she had the inside on all the clubs. So any time I wanted a job, I just called her. I got it right away.
How many different clubs were you...
If you don’t mind my asking, what would you make for a week in one of these clubs at the time?
Oh, I don’t know. Not much. Maybe 125 bucks, something like that.
That you’d clear, and then you’d pay the guys in your band what, $75 or something...
Whatever they’d make. $50. Some of them didn’t make any money at all.
